L1 mail.c:435 is unreachable on the reference: store_mail's 64-bit size guard aborts every send (src/mail.c:258-263; src/mail.h:50,84-104; Zach's 2026-10-26 option-b ruling, PF-066), so no received letter can exist and read_delete's header cannot be rendered. The port keeps the functional 32-bit behaviour as the approved divergence. The earlier oracle-green claim on mail-read-header-depth did not exercise this path: its C transcript is the empty-mail refusal (docs/fidelity/evidence/l1-2026-11-14/mail-read-header-show.txt). With the mail store unaligned at boot, no_mail is set in both engines and the assigned postmaster answers check with only 'Sorry, the mail system is having technical difficulties.'; fault-mail-boot compares the block byte-exactly (R1/R2/R5e/R5h).

The port keeps the functional 32-bit behaviour as the approved divergence; the empty-mail refusal is proven separately by mail.receive-empty-refusal, and the earlier mail-read-header vehicle actually captured the empty refusal (docs/fidelity/evidence/l1-2026-11-14/mail-read-header-show.txt).
